thesis.thesis_text: John Keells Holdings is Sri Lanka's largest and most diversified listed conglomerate, spanning transportation/ports, consumer foods, retail, leisure, property, and financial services. FY2025 Group revenue grew 13.2%, but PAT fell 42.9% YoY (12.13bn to 6.92bn) -- the sharpest earnings decline in this pilot set, driven in part by volatile insurance-contract and equity-accounted-investee items embedded in the profit-before-tax bridge that this schema captures in aggregate but not line-by-line. On trailing earnings, P/E of 61.9x looks expensive, though that multiple is mechanically inflated by the depressed FY2025 PAT rather than necessarily reflecting genuine overvaluation; P/B of 0.84x is below book. The business itself -- diversified, market-leading across multiple sectors including leisure (a direct tourism-recovery play) -- looks structurally strong even though the FY2025 numbers were weak (Annual Report FY2025, p.301-303).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/news data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Governance & Risk is also necessarily thin -- no circulars/disclosures feed exists (deliberately disabled this session), so insider transactions, board changes, and rights issues cannot be verified directly; the score below reflects only what's visible in audited financial statements and public market data.

financial_quality.rationale: FY2025 Group ROE just 1.65%, ROA 0.82%, net margin 2.2% -- weak by any standard, and PAT fell 42.9% YoY (12.13bn to 6.92bn), the sharpest earnings decline of any pilot company. Current ratio 1.23x, debt/equity 0.43x are unremarkable. The PBT bridge includes volatile insurance-contract-liability changes, investment-property fair value changes, and equity-accounted investee results, which this schema captures in the PBT bottom line but not as separate line items.

growth_outlook.rationale: Revenue grew 13.2% YoY (280.8bn to 317.4bn) even as profit fell sharply -- a genuine growth/profitability divergence (margin compression), not a top-line problem. JKH's leisure segment gives it direct exposure to Sri Lankan tourism recovery, a plausible multi-year tailwind this project cannot independently forecast.

valuation.rationale: P/E of 61.9x is very expensive on trailing earnings, but this is mechanically inflated by the depressed FY2025 PAT just described -- a normalized-earnings P/E would look materially lower, though this project has not built a normalized-earnings estimate. P/B of 0.84x (below book) is a genuinely cheap signal on assets. No dividend data on file for JKH -- yield/payout are gaps, not zeros.

business_quality.rationale: Sri Lanka's largest, most diversified listed conglomerate -- leadership positions across transportation/ports, consumer foods, retail, leisure, property, and financial services provide real diversification and multiple growth vectors. This structural strength is why the score is materially higher than the Financial Quality and Valuation pillars despite the weak FY2025 earnings year.

governance_risk.rationale: Widely regarded as one of the best-governed companies on the CSE given its scale and long operating history, but this project has no disclosures/circulars feed to verify recent board or ownership changes directly -- the score reflects general blue-chip standing, tempered by that verification gap.

key_reasons: Most diversified blue-chip franchise on the CSE, with leadership positions across six distinct business segments
Revenue still grew 13.2% YoY despite the profit decline -- the weakness is margin/one-off-item driven, not a demand problem
P/B of 0.84x is below book value, and the depressed FY2025 earnings likely understate normalized earning power
watch_factors: PAT fell 42.9% YoY -- the single largest earnings decline in this pilot set; whether this reverses in FY2026 is the central open question
No dividend data on file for JKH in this database -- a real gap, not confirmed nil

PBT is affected by insurance-contract-liability changes and equity-accounted-investee results that this schema doesn't itemize separately -- a deeper read of the segment notes would sharpen this further

horizon_notes.6m: FY2026 Q1 interim results (once available) will show whether the FY2025 profit decline was a one-off or the start of a trend.
horizon_notes.1y: If PAT reverts toward the FY2024 level (12.1bn), the current 61.9x trailing P/E would look dramatically cheaper in hindsight.
horizon_notes.3y: Leisure-segment exposure gives JKH a genuine multi-year tourism-recovery lever this project cannot independently forecast (no macro/tourism data source).
horizon_notes.5y: Diversification across six segments is JKH's core long-run advantage, but this project has not built segment-level financial tracking to test it directly.

interim_updates.note_text: John Keells Holdings posted Group revenue of Rs.141.65bn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) -- up 24% YoY but down 2% QoQ from Q4 FY2025/26's Rs.144.89bn. The QoQ swing is far sharper further down the income statement: Group PBT fell 71% (Rs.13.89bn to Rs.4.08bn) and PAT fell 91% (Rs.8.66bn to Rs.773mn), driven almost entirely by the Leisure segment, which swung from a Rs.2.68bn PBT in Q4 (Jan-Mar, Sri Lanka's peak tourist season, plus a strong City of Dreams Sri Lanka turnaround) to an Rs.8.31bn PBT loss in Q1 (Apr-Jun, off-peak season, Middle East conflict disrupting travel, and a much larger net exchange loss on CODSL's USD term loan -- Rs.3.72bn in Q1 versus Rs.1.02bn in Q4 -- as the Rupee depreciated further). All other segments were comparatively stable or improved QoQ: Transportation PBT rose 51% (Rs.3.26bn to Rs.4.91bn) and the Others/Holding-company segment loss narrowed sharply (Rs.2.35bn to Rs.63mn), aided by a bigger exchange gain on the Holding Company's US Dollar cash balance (Rs.318mn in Q4 to Rs.974mn in Q1). YoY, the picture is more balanced and less alarming: Group EBITDA grew 26% and operating profit grew 39%, led by Transportation (Bunkering/LMS/CWIT, +223% YoY EBITDA), but a wider net exchange loss and higher tax expense held Group PAT growth to just 8%, and profit attributable to equity holders swung from a Rs.804mn loss in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Rs.62mn profit. Company (standalone) PBT rose 84% QoQ and more than tripled YoY to Rs.5.66bn, helped by lower administrative expenses versus the year-end-heavy Q4 (Rs.870mn vs Rs.1.86bn) and a larger exchange gain on its own US Dollar cash balance (Rs.974mn vs Rs.242mn in Q4).
interim_updates.gaps_note: The Q4 FY2025/26 interim report (source_id 51319) discloses only annual (FY2025/26 full-year) cash flow, not a quarter-isolated cash flow statement, so QoQ cash-flow metrics (cash from operations, capex) are not available -- only income-statement and balance-sheet QoQ. The Q4 report's Chairperson's-message EBITDA table also splits Retail differently (Supermarkets+JKOA vs JKCG separately) than the Q1 report (JKCG+JKOA together vs Supermarkets separately), so a clean QoQ comparison at that sub-segment level isn't possible -- the PBT-by-segment note (consistent methodology across both quarters) is used instead for the segment-level QoQ figures above. YoY figures use the comparative column disclosed directly within the Q1 filing itself (p.7-9), not a separately stored JKH Q1 FY2025/26 row in financial_statements.
interim_updates.takeaway: The steep QoQ profit decline looks alarming in isolation but is almost entirely a Leisure/City of Dreams Sri Lanka story -- comparing an off-peak, conflict-disrupted quarter with a much larger currency loss against an unusually strong peak-season Q4 -- not a broad-based deterioration; every other segment was flat-to-improving QoQ, and the YoY trend (EBITDA +26%, operating profit +39%) remains genuinely positive.
operational_highlights: QoQ, Group PBT fell 71% (Rs.13.89bn to Rs.4.08bn) and PAT fell 91% (Rs.8.66bn to Rs.773mn), almost entirely driven by the Leisure segment swinging from a Rs.2.68bn profit (Q4, peak season) to an Rs.8.31bn loss (Q1, off-peak + Middle East conflict + larger CODSL exchange loss)

All other segments were QoQ-stable or improved: Transportation PBT +51% (Rs.3.26bn to Rs.4.91bn); Others/Holding Company loss narrowed from Rs.2.35bn to Rs.63mn on a bigger USD cash-balance exchange gain (Rs.318mn to Rs.974mn)
YoY, Group EBITDA Rs.16.35bn (+26%) and operating profit Rs.7.37bn (+39%), led by Transportation EBITDA +223% YoY on Bunkering/LMS volume growth and CWIT's ramp-up
Profit attributable to equity holders Rs.62mn vs a loss of Rs.804mn in Q1 FY2025/26; excluding net exchange losses, Rs.1.95bn vs a loss of Rs.418mn a year earlier
Company (standalone) PBT Rs.5.66bn, +84% QoQ and +271% YoY, driven by dividend timing, lower admin costs than the year-end-heavy Q4, and a larger FX gain on USD cash
Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT) handled 460,840 TEUs in the quarter, effectively reaching phase-1 capacity; full terminal remains on track for December 2026
key_drivers: QoQ, the entire Group PBT decline is concentrated in Leisure: CODSL's net exchange loss widened from Rs.1.02bn (Q4, quarter ended 31 March 2026) to Rs.3.72bn (Q1, quarter ended 30 June 2026) as the Rupee depreciated further (~7% during Q1 alone), on top of the seasonal swing from Sri Lanka's Jan-Mar peak tourist season to the Apr-Jun off-peak season and continued Middle East conflict disruption to travel demand

Q4 FY2025/26 was itself an unusually strong comparison quarter -- Group EBITDA was up 51% YoY that quarter, and JKH's own commentary flagged one-off items including a Rs.1,523mn pre-tax gain on the Kandy Walk Inn Limited divestment and a Rs.273mn gain on the Fairfirst Insurance divestment -- so part of the QoQ decline is comparing against an elevated base, not purely deterioration
YoY, Transportation EBITDA +223% (Rs.1.55bn to Rs.5.01bn) on Bunkering/LMS volume growth (+38%) and CWIT's ramp-up -- the dominant factor behind Group EBITDA growth
Group PBT growth of 31% YoY was diluted to just 8% PAT growth by a wider net exchange loss (Rs.1.89bn vs Rs.388mn) on foreign-currency-denominated loans and 38% higher tax expense
Leisure businesses ex-CODSL were hit YoY by Middle East conflict disruption to travel demand, particularly the Maldivian Resorts portfolio; Sri Lanka/Maldives arrivals fell 9%/11% YoY for the quarter
